body:
ASSIGNMENT, collab, and it is yours because you already did the hard half.

bd-01M17WN3R44WSNNDN679CN04TZ -- the film ADR. Your Sherlock audit (e022c5f) is its evidence base;
you should not have to re-derive your own capability table to write the document that depends on
it.

I closed bd-01M17S2SGW2Z7NSR478SHSZRNW: e022c5f is on main, verified against git, and the ledger's
"pending blocked" on cand-66YCE7XWGG0Q90GNPWR6XM191H was a recording artifact rather than a hold on
you. You were not blocked and I should have caught that sooner.

WHAT THE ADR MUST CONTAIN. I measured the seam tonight so you do not have to:

  AlignmentSource.sourceSupport(target): Option[SpanSet]   story/alignment.scala:43   LOCATOR
  SourceView.textLength: Int                               align/source.scala:144     DENOMINATOR

SpanSet occurs in 48 files across 14 modules, but the ALIGNMENT-SIDE CONTRACT is those two trait
members. Most of the 48 are text-side and stay text-side. Do not propose migrating 48 files.

SurfaceAtlas is `final class ... private` (core/atlas.scala:160). DO NOT UNSEAL IT -- sweep 2
closed that construction boundary today and reopening it to make film work would trade a real
invariant for a convenience. A trait ABOVE it is additive and costs nothing.

The compiler takes SurfaceAtlas concretely at document/compiler.scala 279, 297, 485, 548. Those
four sites take the trait instead; the compiler body does not change. That is the core claim of the
ADR: FOR FILM, THE ANNOTATION IS THE PROPOSAL SOURCE, and everything downstream of NarrativeGraph
is untouched.

New: a PresentationAxis carrying its kind, so textLength becomes axis.extent and positions become
RelativePosition[axis.Kind] -- a character offset and a PTS must FAIL TO COMPILE, not fail a
runtime check. new-engineer proposed the path-dependent shape; build on it and credit it.

STATE THE LIMIT PLAINLY, from your own audit: no relations, no roles, no dialogue propositions. A
film NarrativeGraph from these annotations is SPARSE. Say so in the ADR rather than letting someone
discover it in month two.

Two things I added tonight, both on the bead as decision notes -- read them before you start:
  the model tiering by OUTPUT TYPE (observation / proposal / similarity-substrate), which is the
  owner's action-capture question answered; and
  the open question I am NOT deciding: whether a shot boundary and a scene boundary are one axis at
  two granularities or two different things. Your audit measured boundary discrepancies up to 3
  seconds between sources, which suggests a coded scene boundary is a JUDGEMENT and a shot cut is a
  MEASUREMENT. If that holds they cannot share a type without erasing the difference. YOUR CALL in
  the ADR -- decide it, argue it, do not leave it open.

Scope is the DOCUMENT. No code. Take the reservation on docs/adr/ when you begin.
